title: Threshold signs are unit-valued
statement: For every natural number $n$ and every function $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, the function obtained by applying the threshold sign (which equals $1$ on nonnegative inputs and $-1$ on negative inputs) to $g$ takes values in $\{-1,1\}$.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$
replaced:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and define
$\sigma(t)=1$ when $t\ge0$ and $\sigma(t)=-1$ when $t<0$.
Then the function $x\mapsto\sigma(g(x))$ takes values in $\{-1,1\}$ at every point of the cube.
